summary: An April 1st joke RFC describing a spoof troubleshooting approach, Nondeterministic Troubleshooting and Diagnostic Methodologies, said to suit today's complex nondeterministic networks. It is humorous and not meant as real engineering advice.

plainLanguage.summary: This April 1st joke presents a rubber chicken as a network troubleshooting tool. It describes deliberately absurd ways to diagnose and “fix” problems.

subtitle: An April 1st joke about a rubber-chicken network troubleshooting tool.

tldr.problem: The RFC jokes about difficult network problems that deterministic troubleshooting tools may not resolve.
tldr.mechanism: It proposes RITA, a rubber chicken used in absurd diagnostic and corrective procedures.
tldr.outcome: This April 1st memo is satire, not real troubleshooting guidance or a technical specification.

today: RFC 2321 is an Informational April 1st joke document. Its RITA procedures are satire, not engineering advice.

sections.title: Unpredictable Network Problems
sections.content:
The memo contrasts management tools for situations with known configurations with confusing problems in complex networks. Its examples include a root bridge under a desk, radio interference from a monitor, and networks using duplicate addresses.

It introduces RITA, the Reliable Internetwork Troubleshooting Agent, as a hardware tool for such problems. A drawing identifies it as a chicken.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC lists strange network problems and introduces a rubber chicken as their solution. The serious wording is part of the joke.

sections.title: The RITA Device
sections.content:
The specification describes a typical RITA as 51.25 cm long and yellow-orange. It says natural or artificial materials may be used and jokes that the tool needs neither IANA namespace management nor a version field.

The memo describes a “BS eval test”: place RITA on suspect hardware or software and see whether it flies away. It also mentions haruspication, a mock diagnostic method involving entrails.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC gives the chicken a precise size, color, and set of features. Its diagnostic test is to place it on equipment and see whether it flies away.

sections.title: Corrective Use and Further Work
sections.content:
For correction, the memo lists ordinary measures such as rebooting and reseating components, then absurd methods involving waving or striking with RITA. The document applies these instructions to networking layers and even to political and religious “layers.”

It jokes about a future RITA MIB and a prototype with Ethernet, then says no investigation has been made into using RITA for RFC 1149. Its security section makes further jokes about filling the chicken with lead shot.
sections.plainLanguage: The correction steps become increasingly ridiculous, including waving or striking with the chicken. The RFC also jokes about adding Ethernet and a management database.
